Read the result of step 13 (your predecessor's findings F1-F5) and the result of step 14 (the rework). Check yourself:
(1) F1 is really closed: SV-9g serves a /3 file with leads enabled and no whatsapp and expects whatsapp null as the second key of leads in ru, kk, en and through publicQuestionnaire; the oracle is a literal. Apply the mutant yourself (public-data.js gives undefined for a missing whatsapp; also a variant that gives "" and a variant that omits whatsapp when it is a number) on a scratch copy: each must turn a test red.
(2) F2 and F3 are closed: LK-5a has the two new desk cases with the right literal lines, LK-4b the tags "A BCD" and "ab cd"; mutants MU70b and the swapped order (class check before count check) are red in those tests.
(3) The rework changed nothing but tools/test (diff against the tag and the sha256 of tools/src equal 129787a2...) and weakened nothing: compare the diff of the two touched test files with the state after step 12 (the test( and assert. counts did not fall).
(4) Because this is a second pass, try at least EIGHT new mutants of your own that neither the design list nor the first gate used, aimed at the whole new logic (the check order inside validate, the keys order of the public answer, the lang-check rules for the /3 mode, the fallback look, the clamp of deskForQuestion, the frozen objects, the ctx.line/ctx.list move in shape.js, the limits). Every non-equivalent mutant must turn at least one test red; report equivalent mutants with a reason. One scratch run at a time, restore after each.
(5) Run `npm run check` once in the live tree: green (2044 tests expected), sha256 of tools/src unchanged.
Verdict PASS or FAIL with findings (severity, file, line, fix). Low findings go to the follow-up list; only a surviving non-equivalent mutant on a stated criterion or a real defect makes FAIL. In your handoff text never list project names or machine paths (say "the traces list").
